title: DOiT: Better Money-Flow Ranking Can Coexist with Worse Account Selection in Anti-Money Laundering Review
abstract: arXiv:2611.27809v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Anti-money laundering (AML) review selects suspicious accounts and reconstructs transfers. Downstream graph neural networks (GNNs) rank money-flow evidence but may also reorder the account queue. DOiT separates these decisions at equal review capacity: account selection determines where graph investigation starts. Across AMLWorld and AMLNet, GNN reordering harms higher-yield upstream orders but helps lower-yield ones. On AMLWorld, this harm coexists with higher transaction average precision (AP) in dimension-matched, per-run decoders, demonstrating separable ranking abilities. At small capacities, positive neighbors can displace a denser upstream prefix and lower yield; replacement costs fall as that prefix is exhausted, allowing the preferred order to reverse. A restricted-access synthetic benchmark informed by real transaction patterns reproduces this separation and validation-based upstream preservation. Capacity-matched combination

translated_title: DOiT：在反洗钱审查中，更好的资金流排序可以与更差的账户选择共存
translated_abstract: 反洗钱（AML）审查需要选择可疑账户并重构转账链条。下游图神经网络（GNN）会对资金流证据进行排序，但同时也可能对账户队列进行重新排序。DOiT 在同等审查容量下将这两种决策分离：账户选择决定了图调查的起点位置。在 AMLWorld 和 AMLNet 数据集上的实验表明，GNN 的重排序会损害高收益的上游排序，但对低收益排序有所帮助。在 AMLWorld 上，这种损害与维度匹配的、逐次运行的解码器中更高的交易平均精度（AP）并存，证明了这两种排序能力是可分离的。在小容量情况下，正邻居样本可能取代更密集的上游前缀并降低收益；随着该前缀被逐渐耗尽，替换成本下降，导致偏好排序可能发生逆转。一个基于真实交易模式构建的受限访问合成基准重现了这种分离现象以及基于验证的上游保持效果。容量匹配的组合方式……
tldr: DOiT 揭示了反洗钱审查中一个关键现象：即使 GNN 重排序提升了交易资金流的排序精度（更高的 AP），也可能损害上游账户选择的质量，因此应在同等审查容量下将资金流排序与账户选择这两种决策分离处理。
en_tdlr: DOiT shows that better money-flow ranking (higher transaction AP) can coexist with worse account selection in AML review, and proposes separating these two decisions at equal review capacity to prevent GNN reordering from harming upstream account selection quality.
